'''Pix''' was a [[Gender|male]] [[tooka]] [[cat]] who, during the [[Imperial Era]], was owned by a [[Pix's owner|human]] on the [[Core Worlds]] [[planet]] [[Coruscant]]. In [[1 BBY]], Pix and its owner visited a [[Unidentified park|park]] where, after being allowed to go for a run, the tooka came across the [[Death|dead]] body of [[Imperial Security Bureau]] [[ISB Supervisor|supervisor]] [[Lonni Jung]]. Pix sniffed Jung's body before being called back to its owner.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Want to go for a run?|Pix's owner, to Pix|audio=Pix2-MakeItStop.flac|<ref name="Make It Stop" />}}
[[File:PixAndOwner-MakeItStop.png|thumb|right|275px|Pix and its owner (right) went for a walk to a park on Coruscant.]]
Pix was a [[Gender|male]] [[tooka]] [[cat]] owned by a [[Pix's owner|human]] on<ref name="Make It Stop" /> the [[Core Worlds]] [[planet]]<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]''</ref> [[Coruscant]] during the [[Imperial Era]]. In [[1 BBY]], Pix and<ref name="Make It Stop" /> its<ref name="Make It Stop audio" /> owner went for a walk and visited a Coruscant<ref name="Make It Stop" /> [[Unidentified park|park]] next to a reflection [[Water|pool]]<ref name="Make It Stop audio" /> within [[Imperial City]]. After their arrival, the owner told Pix it was a good boy before crouching down and taking the cat's leash off while asking the tooka if it wanted to go for a run.<ref name="Make It Stop" />

In response, Pix meowed before<ref name="Make It Stop" /> scampering<ref name="Make It Stop audio" /> over to a figure sat on a bench—the [[Death|dead]] [[Imperial Security Bureau]]<ref name="Make It Stop" /> [[ISB Supervisor|supervisor]]<ref name="Trivia">{{SW|url=news/andor-trivia-guide-week-4|text=Secrets from the Set of ''Andor'' Season 2: Week 4 Trivia}}</ref> [[Lonni Jung]]—and began sniffing his body and meowing. The tooka's owner then called to<ref name="Make It Stop" /> his<ref name="Make It Stop audio" /> cat, telling Pix to come to him. After the tooka looked away from Jung's body and sniffed again, the owner repeated his call for the cat to go to him, and Pix<ref name="Make It Stop" /> wandered<ref name="Make It Stop audio" /> away from Jung.<ref name="Make It Stop" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Listen3|Pix3-MakeItStop.flac|Pix meowing}}
Pix had [[Color|dark brown]] skin, cream and brown [[Hair|fur]] with darker fur on its [[ear]]s, and light blue [[eye]]s.<ref name="Databank" />

==Equipment==
The tooka wore a gray-brown collar.<ref name="Databank" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|You would be so happy to know how many meetings there were on that stupid dog. I think I approved three different dogs. Like, "Yeah, that dog is fine for me." "Okay, that dog is also fine for me." Then people kept raising their hand: "I think it looks like a raccoon."|Tony Gilroy|<ref name="Vulture">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vulture.com/article/tony-gilroy-andor-star-wars-rogue-one-interview.html|text='Before Anyone Else Defines It, I'm Going to Define It' ''Andor'' creator Tony Gilroy reflects on five years inside the ''Star Wars'' universe.|author=VanArendonk, Kathryn|date=2025-05-16|work=[[Wikipedia:Vulture (website)|''Vulture'']]|archivedate=20250519093736}}</ref>}}
[[File:AndorSeason2-Poster.jpg|thumb|right|180px|''Andor'' Season 2 marked the first appearance of Pix.]]
Pix first appeared in "[[Make It Stop]],"<ref name="Make It Stop" /> the tenth episode in the [[Andor Season 2|second season]] of the live-action [[Disney+]] series [[Star Wars: Andor|''Andor'']],<ref name="Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/andor/season-2-episode-10-episode-guide|text="Make It Stop" Episode Guide | Andor A Star Wars Story}}</ref> which aired on [[May 13]], [[2025]].<ref name="Trailer">{{SW|url=news/andor-season-2-teaser-trailer-key-art-reveal|text=First ''Andor A Star Wars Story'' Teaser Trailer and Poster Revealed}}</ref> During production, [[Tony Gilroy]]—the series' creator—approved three different creatures for use that he referred to as "dogs," one of which ultimately was the tooka. As other production members disagreed with the tooka's aesthetic, with one describing it as a "raccoon," the creature was repeatedly sent back for further revisions upon request of Tony's brother, art designer [[John Gilroy]].<ref name="Vulture" />

Further, several different sounds were approved for the tooka, and what to name it for the credits was discussed.<ref name="Vulture" /> Ultimately the cat was named after a deceased dog of one of the series' visual effects artists.<ref name="Trivia" />
